title: Generator delegation (yield*)
description: `yield*` delegates iteration to another iterable — generators, arrays, strings — letting you compose iterators without manual loops.

notes: `yield* iterable` is shorthand for `for (const v of iterable) yield v;` — including completion handling.
The delegated iterable can be a generator, array, string, Set, Map, or anything with `[Symbol.iterator]`.
`yield` (no star) on an iterable would emit the iterable itself as one value — use `yield*` to flatten.

options: Yields the iterable as a single value
Yields each value of the iterable one at a time
Throws unless the iterable is a generator
questions.explain: yield* delegates iteration — it yields each value the inner iterable produces.

questions.q: Which of these is `yield* [1, 2]` roughly equivalent to?
Can `yield*` delegate to a non-generator iterable like an array or string?
options: No — only generator functions can be delegated to

questions.q: Inside `function* outer() { yield 0; yield* [1, 2]; yield 3; }`, what is `[...outer()]`?

exercises.prompt: Use yield* to delegate to an inner generator.
Delegate to an array literal directly.

L3.prompt: Write `function* combined()` that delegates to two inner generators: `evens()` yielding 2,4 and `odds()` yielding 1,3. Order them evens-then-odds. Log `[...combined()].join('-')`.
hints: Spread the generator and call `.join('-')` on the resulting array.
